title: Introduce region-aware admission controller and sandboxed policy runner
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The smart routing layer occasionally creates cross-region contention and long tail latencies when policy evaluation stalls or when one busy region saturates shared queues. Root causes observed during incidents: (1) policy evaluation runs synchronously on the hotpath and can block request threads when a policy consult hangs, (2) the global admission queue permits bursty cross-region demand that starves regional capacity, and (3) lack of a sandboxed execution boundary for third-party/adaptive policies means a single slow decision can cascade.
goal: Introduce a lightweight region-aware admission controller that enforces per-region inflight limits and backpressure semantics, and extract policy evaluation into a sandboxed worker pool with bounded latency windows and feature-flagged timeouts. Reduce P95/P99 routing latency and eliminate policy-hang-induced thread starvation while preserving current routing correctness and fallback semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Per-region inflight limiter enforced behind a toggle; no global queue starvation observed in synthetic load tests
Policy runner moved off hotpath into sandboxed worker pool with configurable timeout (default 50ms) and graceful fallback path on timeout
End-to-end tests demonstrating behavior under region surge: requests are admitted or retried with documented metrics
No increase in error-rate for existing canary customers during staged rollout
Tracing shows policy execution spans isolated to sandbox workers and not contributing to request critical path latency
implementation_steps: Design admission controller API and config (per-region max_inflight, burst_multiplier, retry_backoff) -- design doc in Confluence
Introduce sandboxed policy runner service: bounded goroutine/worker pool with per-eval deadline and enforced cancellation
Add feature flag to switch routing layer to use admission controller and sandboxed runner
Instrument metrics: region_inflight_count, admission_rejections, policy_timeout_count, policy_duration_histogram
Create integration harness that replays production routing traffic to validate behavior under surge
Canary roll: enable toggle for a non-critical region for 48 hours, monitor P95/P99 and rejection metrics, then widen rollout
Cleanup: remove legacy synchronous policy hotpath and dead config after stable rollout
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect per-region limits could throttle healthy traffic. Mitigation: conservative default (high enough to avoid customer-visible throttling) and autoscaling-friendly settings; rollout behind toggle
Risk: Policy timeouts degrade result quality. Mitigation: implement adaptive timeout tuning per-policy and circuit-breaker-style fallback to cached/cheap policy result or default decision
Risk: Added complexity in routing logic increases maintenance overhead. Mitigation: thorough docs, metrics, and a small public interface for the admission controller to reduce coupling
